identity.name: Hospitaller Tripoli
alt_names: Tripoli under the Knights of Malta
Order of St John at Tripoli

land.text: Tripoli, held by Spain since 1510 and given to the Order with Malta and Gozo

predecessors.note: After the expulsion from Rhodes in 1522 the Knights 'negotiated with Charles V, who offered Tripoli, Malta, and Gozo'.

land.text: Tripoli, which 'surrendered on 14 August' 1551 to Sinan Pasha and Dragut

successors.note: The infobox dates the Ottoman conquest to 15 August 1551, the text to 14 August; the city 'remained under Ottoman rule until Italy captured it in 1911'.

capitals.name: Tripoli
capitals.note: The Order's headquarters were at Birgu on Malta; Tripoli had a separate governor: Gaspare de Sanguessa (1530-1531) first, Jean de Valette from 1546 and Gaspard de Vallier (1551) last. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the walled city of Tripoli, outside which the Hospitallers destroyed the el-Cadi tower built by Tajura's ruler

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Tajura, 'under Ottoman influence', gave daily skirmishes in 1539; the Order's hold outside the walls is never described. The 25 km circle is the grid's minimum.

ledger.note: 25 July 1530: the Order takes Tripoli. The Hospitallers 'accepted Tripoli, Malta and Gozo as a fief on 23 March 1530' and 'took control of the city on 25 July' (infobox: established 25 July 1530).

14 August 1551: Tripoli capitulates. 'Tripoli capitulated on 14 August 1551' after six days of bombardment (infobox: siege 8-14 August 1551); 'The Ottomans and the residents of Tajura began their siege of Tripoli on 8 August'; on 15 August part of the garrison and the knights left for Malta on ships provided by the French ambassador. The Hospitaller Tripoli page has a two-week siege and 'the city surrendered on 14 August' (infobox: Ottoman conquest 15 August).
1551: Hospitaller rule ends. The city 'remained under Ottoman rule until Italy captured it in 1911'; the Order raided Tripolitania in 1552 in an attempt to recapture it.

wars.name: Ottoman siege of Tripoli
wars.outcome: Sinan Pasha and Dragut, with Murad Agha's Tajura forces, besieged Tripoli from 8 August 1551; Gaspard de Vallier capitulated on 14 August after six days of bombardment; 200 Muslim auxiliaries were executed and the rest of the garrison enslaved, except the knights.
wars.note: The Hospitaller Tripoli page gives a two-week siege and the infobox 15 August.

certainty.note: One walled city; the page gives no extent and the 25 km circle is the grid's minimum.

notes: Cliopatria has no Hospitaller row: the Hafsid Dynasty row carries Tripolitania to 1551 (Hafsid dossier, note 2). Skirmishes with Tajura (under Aydin Reis, who built the el-Cadi tower about a mile outside the walls, destroyed by Georg Schilling von Cannstatt, no year) are on the page, with March-June 1539 as the only year implied; no war is entered for them. The page also has Dragut capture the galley La Catarinetta carrying 7,000 scudi (no date), the 1559-1560 Battle of Djerba and Dragut as beylerbey of Tripoli in 1556; none touches the Order's land.
